source_title: Chilli Production Technology and Plant Protection
section: Sucking Pests - Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) and Leaf Curl
text: Whitefly nymphs and adults suck sap from the undersides of leaves, secreting honeydew which attracts sooty mould. More critically, whitefly acts as the insect vector transmitting the Chilli Leaf Curl Virus, causing severe upward leaf curling, puckering, stunted bush growth, and total yield loss if unmanaged. Non-chemical management: Erect yellow sticky traps @ 10-15 traps per acre at canopy level to monitor and trap whitefly adults. Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Neem oil 1500 ppm @ 5 ml per litre of water at early infestation. Chemical intervention: When pest intensity crosses ETL (5-8 whiteflies per leaf), spray Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.25 g per litre of water (18.75 g to 19 g per 15-litre knapsack pump) or Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.2 g per litre of water (3 g per 15-litre pump). Safety: Spray during morning or evening hours with calm air. Wear protective gloves and face mask; never spray against wind. Waiting period (PHI): 15 days before harvesting green chillies.

source_title: Chilli Production Technology and Plant Protection
text: Thrips lacerate the tender leaf surface and suck oozing sap, causing upward curling of leaf margins, boat-shaped leaf deformity, crinkling, and bronze or silvery discoloration on the ventral surface. Non-chemical management: Install blue sticky traps @ 10-15 per acre. Avoid excessive nitrogenous fertilizers. Chemical management: Spray Fipronil 5% SC @ 2 ml per litre of water (30 ml per 15-litre spray tank) or Spinosad 45% SC @ 0.3 ml per litre of water (4.5 ml per 15-litre spray tank). Safety: Alternate chemical groups to prevent rapid resistance buildup. Pre-harvest waiting period is 12 days.

source_title: Chilli Production Technology and Plant Protection
section: Fungal Diseases - Anthracnose, Dieback and Fruit Rot (Colletotrichum capsici)
text: Symptoms include dark brown sunken circular spots with concentric rings on ripe fruits, followed by dry rot. Twigs die back from the tip downward, with withered branches turning white with black dot-like acervuli. Non-chemical management: Use disease-free seeds; treat seed with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed before nursery sowing. Destroy diseased crop debris and remove infected ripe pods promptly. Chemical management: Spray Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml per litre of water (15 ml per 15-litre tank) or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 ml per litre of water (7.5 ml per 15-litre tank) at 10-14 days intervals upon symptom onset. Safety: Wear full-body overalls and protective goggles during spraying. Waiting period: 10 days.

source_title: Chilli Production Technology and Plant Protection
section: Soil-borne Diseases - Damping-off and Collar Rot (Pythium / Phytophthora)
text: Water-soaked lesions develop at the collar region of young seedlings, leading to rotting, softening of tissues, and toppling over of seedlings in nurseries or freshly transplanted fields. Non-chemical management: Prepare raised nursery beds 15 cm high with proper drainage. Avoid stagnant water and overwatering. Chemical management: Drench the nursery bed and root zone with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g per litre of water (45 g per 15-litre can/pump) or Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2 g per litre of water (30 g per 15-litre pump). Safety: Do not apply in direct midday sunshine. Keep livestock away from treated areas.

Pink bollworm larvae enter tender flower buds and squares, webbing the petals together to form characteristic 'rosette flowers' (Domkalya). Larvae bore into developing green bolls, feeding on developing seeds and staining the lint brown or yellow. Non-chemical management: Regularly collect and destroy rosette flowers and dropped squares. Install 5 pheromone traps per acre with Gossyplure lures for monitoring, and 8-10 traps per acre for mass trapping. Chemical intervention at ETL (8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive days or 10% damaged green bolls): Spray Profenophos 50% EC @ 2 ml per litre of water (30 ml per 15-litre knapsack pump) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4 g per litre of water (6 g per 15-litre pump). Safety: Do not spray synthetic pyrethroids repeatedly as they induce resurgence of sucking pests. PHI: 30 days.

section: Sucking Pests - Aphids (Aphis gossypii) and Resistance Management
text: Aphids (Mava) colonize the lower surface of tender leaves and shoots, sucking sap and causing downward leaf cupping. They excrete sweet honeydew leading to black sooty mold fungus on lower foliage. Resistance warning: Repeated sprays of organophosphates or synthetic pyrethroids trigger rapid pesticide resistance. Non-chemical management: Stop indiscriminate chemical spraying immediately. Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) @ 50 g/L or conserve natural predators like ladybird beetles and chrysoperla. Chemical management: If aphid population exceeds 15-20% affected plants, spray Flonicamid 50 WG @ 0.3 g per litre of water (4.5 g per 15-litre spray tank) or Dinotefuran 20% SG @ 0.3 g per litre of water (4.5 g per 15-litre tank). Safety: Ensure thorough coverage of lower leaf surface using hollow cone nozzle. PHI: 25 days.

section: Fungal Diseases - Grey Mildew / Dahiya Disease (Ramularia areola)
text: Characterized by irregular angular pale green or yellowish spots on upper leaf surfaces, with frosty white, powdery fungal sporulation on the lower surface resembling a drenching of curd (Dahiya). Leaves turn prematurely brown and shed. Non-chemical management: Ensure wider plant spacing to allow sun penetration and air circulation. Remove lower old infected leaves. Chemical management: Spray Wettable Sulphur 80% WP @ 3 g per litre of water (45 g per 15-litre pump) or Kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC @ 1 ml per litre of water (15 ml per 15-litre pump). Safety: Do not spray wettable sulphur when ambient temperature exceeds 35 degrees Celsius to prevent phytotoxicity.

source_title: Package of Practices for Kharif Crops - Rice
section: Fungal Diseases - Brown Spot (Bipolaris oryzae / Helminthosporium)
text: Brown spot produces numerous circular to oval brown spots with a yellow halo resembling sesame seeds on leaf blades and glumes. Severely diseased leaves turn yellow, dry up, and seedlings/tillers become severely blighted, especially under potash deficiency. Non-chemical management: Ensure balanced fertilizer application; avoid excessive nitrogen and rectify potassium deficiency in sandy loam soils. Drain stagnant water and provide fresh irrigation. Chemical management: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml per litre of water (15 ml per 15-litre spray pump) or Tebuconazole 50% + Trifloxystrobin 25% WG (Nativo) @ 0.4 g per litre of water (6 g per 15-litre pump). Safety: Always wear protective rubber gloves and mask. Avoid skin and eye contact. Waiting period: 30 days before harvest.

source_title: Package of Practices for Kharif Crops - Rice
text: Blast produces spindle-shaped lesions on leaves with pointed ends, greyish centres, and dark brown margins. At heading stage, neck blast rots the panicle base turning it black, causing chaffy panicles that snap and break. Non-chemical management: Refrain from applying nitrogen in split doses during cloudy and humid weather. Chemical management: At early symptom detection, spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g per litre of water (9 g per 15-litre spray tank) or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml per litre of water (22.5 ml per 15-litre spray pump). Safety: Spray during morning hours before strong winds develop. Waiting period (PHI): 30 days.

source_title: Package of Practices for Kharif Crops - Rice
section: Insect Pests - Planthoppers and Sucking Pests (BPH / WBPH / Tela)
text: Brown planthopper and white-backed planthopper (Tela) congregate in colonies at the basal stem region just above water level. They suck sap causing tillers to turn yellow and dry up rapidly into circular scorched patches known as 'hopper burn'. Non-chemical management: Create alley pathways (30 cm paths every 2-3 meters) to let sunlight and air into the canopy. Drain flood water from the field for 2-3 days to disturb nymphal colonies. Chemical management: When population exceeds 5-10 hoppers per hill, direct the spray nozzle toward the base of plants. Spray Pymetrozine 50% WDG @ 0.6 g per litre of water (9 g per 15-litre pump) or Triflumezopyrim 10% SC @ 0.5 ml per litre of water (7.5 ml per 15-litre pump). Avoid spraying upper leaf tips as hoppers dwell at plant base. PHI: 21 days.

source_title: Package of Practices for Commercial Vegetable Crops - Tomato
section: Nutritional Disorders - Nitrogen and Calcium Deficiencies
text: Nitrogen deficiency causes uniform pale yellowing (chlorosis) beginning on older lower leaves, while upper young leaves remain smaller and pale green. Stems become thin, fibrous, and growth slows down significantly without any fungal spots or necrotic rings. Calcium deficiency produces 'Blossom End Rot' where the distal blossom end of green fruits develops water-soaked dark sunken leathery rot. Non-chemical management: Do NOT apply chemical pesticides or fungicides for physiological disorders. Incorporate well-rotted farmyard manure (FYM) or vermicompost into the root zone and maintain uniform soil moisture without water stress. Foliar correction: For nitrogen chlorosis, apply foliar spray of 1% Urea (10 g per litre of water, or 150 g per 15-litre spray tank). For calcium deficiency, spray Calcium Nitrate @ 5 g per litre of water (75 g per 15-litre spray tank). Safety: Spray during morning or evening when temperatures are below 30 deg C to avoid leaf scorch. No waiting period required.

source_title: Package of Practices for Commercial Vegetable Crops - Tomato
section: Fungal Diseases - Early Blight and Late Blight (Alternaria / Phytophthora)
text: Early blight causes brown to dark brown circular spots with distinctive concentric target boards on leaves, stems, and fruits. Late blight produces rapid water-soaked greenish-black lesions that rot leaves and green fruits quickly in cool humid conditions with white mold on leaf underside. Non-chemical management: Stake tomato plants to keep foliage off wet soil. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation. Remove infected lower leaves promptly. Chemical management: For early blight, spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g per litre of water (37.5 g per 15-litre pump) or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 ml per litre of water (7.5 ml per 15-litre pump). For late blight, spray Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2 g per litre of water (30 g per 15-litre tank). Safety: Wear protective mask and gloves; wash equipment thoroughly. Waiting period (PHI): 7 days.

source_title: Package of Practices for Commercial Vegetable Crops - Tomato
section: Viral Diseases - Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV transmitted by Whitefly)
text: Infected plants show severe downward and upward curling of leaflets, thick puckering, yellowing of interveinal areas, and severe stunting. Plants infected early produce no marketable fruit. Transmitted solely by the whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci). Non-chemical management: Raise tomato seedlings under 40-mesh nylon insect-proof net in nursery. Install 15 yellow sticky traps per acre. Rogue out and bury virus-infected plants immediately to eliminate field inoculum. Chemical management: Control whitefly vectors by spraying Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.25 g per litre of water (3.75 g per 15-litre tank) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1 ml per litre of water (15 ml per 15-litre tank). Safety: Do not apply insecticides during heavy flowering to safeguard honeybee pollinators. Waiting period: 10 days.
